narrative:
The model determined that you have a 51% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is just over 50%, the bank decided to deny your loan application.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account status was the strongest influence and pushed the decision toward denial. Having a negative balance (under 0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants—only 12.6% of them show this status—whereas most approved borrowers have either no checking account or a positive balance. This signaled higher risk to the model.

The duration you requested worked in your favor. At 12 months it is noticeably shorter than the 19-month average seen among approved loans, which helped pull the prediction back toward approval. The purpose of the loan (domestic appliances) also slightly reduced the risk score, as this is a common and generally lower-risk reason compared with some other categories.

Even though two of the top factors leaned positive for you, the negative signal from your checking account was strong enough to outweigh them and tip the final probability above the approval threshold.

You should focus on clearing or improving your checking account balance, then reapply in a few months with updated information. This single change is likely to have the biggest positive impact on future decisions. (218 words)
